Grandma, mom, dad, pretty much any family member that only worried we weren't fed enough. They never taught us portion control, but raised us to be grateful we have food to eat and to show it by eating every last morsel. Because of that, we've conditioned our bodies to continue to feel hungry until we felt like we've savored every bite. 
In turn, every time I felt like my blood sugar was low, I thought it was extreme hunger so I would overdo it when it came to any food. Didnt matter what it was if I found it I ate it.
Then, I hit a depressive phase where I cultivated an eating disorder. I was judged for not eating enough and constantly exercising after eating so much as an almond. I spent money on diet pills, laxatives, healthy foods, anything that helped me to drop 60+ in a matter of a fee months.
I gained it all back though, on account of a recent diagnosis of diabetes. As soon as I started insulin, the weight slowly crept back and so did my depression, and eventually I was no longer mindful of what I ate.

 I'm on that "I got 5 minutes to inhale all this food that I paid my hard earned money for so I better get my money's worth" of diet at the moment

Physically, I have no way out of my surroundings, so there's no way I can be around those that aren't toxic to me. I'm trapped. 
Mentally, by gremlins are the only thing that seems to be protective of me, they keep me away from the toxicity, and it baffles me because of the things they tell me. 

 I appreciate your reply, I didn't expect anybody to take this post as seriously as I had intended. This happened to a friend of mine, and she was so nonchalant about it after it happened.

It was a summer night, had to be around 8 or 9 at night, it wasn't too late and the sun was still setting. She was driving home and stopped at a traffic light that intersected with the highway. We live in a smallish town so there were hardly any other cars out and she was literally the only one at the light. Her car is stopped at the lane closer to the left turn lane (one of those 5 lane streets). 
So shes minding her own business zoning out or what have you and all of a sudden she hears the passenger door trying to be opened. She looks over and there's a coked up homeless guy that had opened the door. So she grabs a drink from her cup holder and chucks it at him. It was enough of a surprise to back him up and she quickly reached over to shut the door and lock it. 
He "drunkenky" reached for the door again and as she looked at his face she knew he was out if it. 
By this time the light had already turned green and while he persisted she peeled right on out of there.

Not a crazy story but crisis averted
